title: The Alibi of Windrow House
premise: Estate lawyer Sable Winterbourne is summoned to Windrow House to read the will of Edmund Vane, a patriarch who died a year ago — yet the will bears last week's date and names a beneficiary no one can identify: 'the witness.' When an anonymous confession letter arrives postmarked the day after the funeral, Sable realizes the family has been performing grief for a man whose death they may have staged. As the anniversary dinner approaches, Sable uncovers that Edmund faked his death to test his heirs' loyalty, but the plan curdled when one heir used it to commit a real murder. At the anniversary dinner, Sable exposes the killer before the toast is raised, and the true witness — Edmund's disowned daughter, living hidden as the housekeeper — finally comes forward to claim her inheritance.
about_author: Mirabel Reyes spent a decade as a probate clerk in the English countryside, where she collected the strange, whispered histories of great houses and the families who outlived them. She writes mysteries from a converted stable block, convinced that every will is a confession waiting to be read aloud.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Sable Winterbourne arrives at rain-soaked Windrow House to execute a will dated after its subject's death. The Vane family watches him with brittle courtesy. Reading the document, he finds a clause naming an unknown 'witness' as sole beneficiary. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: professional unease sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: Grief, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Sable observes the heirs — eldest son Marcus, brittle widow Constance, and volatile grandson Toby — rehearsing their mourning like actors. He notices the housekeeper, Mrs. Pell, flinch at Edmund's name. A locked study defies the will's instructions. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: creeping suspicion beneath polite surfaces.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: A letter arrives in Edmund's handwriting confessing to 'the thing done in the boathouse,' postmarked the day after his funeral. Sable hides it from the family. Mrs. Pell warns him, quietly, to leave before the anniversary dinner. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable searches the derelict boathouse and finds a ledger of payments signed by all four heirs, dating from before Edmund's death. Someone was being bought into silence. Marcus catches him there and issues a velvet threat. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: isolation; he trusts no one now.

chapters.title: Constance's Version
chapters.summary: Widow Constance, over sherry, offers her account: Edmund was paranoid in his final year, convinced someone meant to bury him alive — figuratively, she insists. Her hands shake. Sable notes she quotes the will's secret clause verbatim, though it was never published. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: pity tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Mrs. Pell's Locked Door
chapters.summary: Sable follows Mrs. Pell to a cottage on the estate edge and glimpses through a window a room kept exactly as someone's bedroom — a woman's, recently lived in. She knows he saw. That night his car's brakes fail on the coast road. POV: alternating Sable and Mrs. Pell. Emotional beat: fear becoming mutual recognition.

chapters.title: Toby's Confession
chapters.summary: Drunk grandson Toby corners Sable, insisting he wrote the confession letter as a joke — then recants, terrified, saying someone paid him to claim it. The payment came in old banknotes, the kind Edmund hoarded. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the mystery multiplying instead of resolving.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Invitations go out for the one-year memorial dinner. Sable discovers a fifth invitation, addressed to 'M. Vane,' returned unopened from a village forty miles away. The local vicar remembers a young woman by that name who left in disgrace twenty years ago. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: hope with a blade hidden in it.

chapters.title: Marcus Ascendant
chapters.summary: Marcus maneuvers to have the contested will voided, revealing he's been managing estate finances for years — and bleeding them. Sable finds falsified transfer records implicating Marcus in draining Edmund's accounts before the death. POV: alternating Sable and Marcus. Emotional beat: the corrupting arithmetic of inheritance.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: In the attic, Sable finds Edmund's private journals: the old man planned his own disappearance to watch what his family would do for money. The final entry breaks off mid-sentence. Mrs. Pell appears behind him and says, 'He didn't finish it because I interrupted him.' POV: Sable. Emotional beat: vertigo — the dead man was watching all along.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Tale
chapters.summary: Mrs. Pell confesses she helped Edmund stage his death and hide in the cottage, believing it a harmless test. But three weeks later Edmund truly vanished — and she received payments to keep silent about both disappearances. POV: Mrs. Pell. Emotional beat: guilt as loyalty's dark twin.

chapters.title: A Body in the Ice House
chapters.summary: Toby, digging where the journal hinted, uncovers remains in the old ice house. The police arrive; the family closes ranks. Dental records are inconclusive — deliberately so, Sable suspects. The anniversary dinner is moved up to control the narrative. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Photograph
chapters.summary: The vicar produces an old photograph: Maren Vane, Edmund's disowned daughter, exiled after accusing her father of something unspeakable. Sable recognizes her jawline in Mrs. Pell's face. The witness everyone swears is dead has been serving them dinner for years. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: revelation as heartbreak.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Sable confronts Mrs. Pell — Maren. She admits she stayed to learn whether her father ever regretted casting her out, and stayed longer to protect the truth of what happened in the boathouse. She saw Marcus there the night Edmund vanished. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth tearing her in two.

chapters.title: The Forged Date
chapters.summary: Forensic examination shows the will's date was altered — by someone with access to Sable's own office supplies. His partnership is threatened; his credentials questioned. Someone inside his firm is working for the Vanes. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: betrayal reaching beyond the house's walls.

chapters.title: Edmund Alive
chapters.summary: Following the payment trail, Sable finds Edmund Vane living under another name in a coastal boarding house — alive, diminished, and frightened of his own children. He confirms Maren's old accusation was true, and that Marcus learned of the staged death and turned it into leverage. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: power curdled into cowardice.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Edmund gives Sable a sealed letter intended for the dinner — his true testament. Returning, Sable is run off the road; the letter is stolen. He survives because Maren followed him. They form an uneasy alliance: belonging found between two outsiders. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: trust kindling in wreckage.

chapters.title: Reconstructing the Testament
chapters.summary: Sable and Maren rebuild the letter's contents from Edmund's journals, the ledger, and the vicar's records. The evidence points to Marcus killing not Edmund but the hired accomplice who knew too much — the body in the ice house. POV: alternating Sable and Maren. Emotional beat: methodical resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Eve of the Dinner
chapters.summary: Constance, confronted quietly, admits she knew Edmund lived and chose comfort over truth — her loyalty purchased with silence. Toby, sober for once, agrees to testify. The house fills with guests, candles, and the smell of a feast laid over a grave. POV: Constance. Emotional beat: complicity examined, remorse arriving late.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: At the anniversary dinner, Marcus rises to propose a toast to his father's memory. Sable interrupts with the reconstructed testament, the ledger, and Maren standing revealed beside him. Marcus denies everything until Toby corroborates — then reaches for the decanter, where he'd hidden the stolen original letter. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: climax; truth spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: What the Witness Saw
chapters.summary: Marcus is arrested. Maren reads her father's real words to the assembled household: regret without absolution. Edmund, brought back under police protection, faces his daughter across the ruins of his design. She does not forgive him, but she claims her name. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: reckoning without easy mercy.

chapters.title: Windrow, After
chapters.summary: Months later, the estate passes to Maren, who opens its grounds to the village rather than sealing them again. Sable, cleared by his firm, keeps the confession letter framed in his office — a reminder that every document is a life. The wind moves through Windrow House like an answer. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: belonging earned, quiet and durable.
